transcript:
[Doctor]: Hi, good afternoon. How are you doing today?

[Patient]: Hi, doctor. Not so great, to be honest.

[Doctor]: I'm sorry to hear that. Can you tell me more about what's been going on?

[Patient]: I've been feeling really depressed for the past two months. It's been really bad.

[Doctor]: I'm very sorry to hear that. Can you describe some of the symptoms you're experiencing?

[Patient]: Sure. I can't sleep at all. I barely get 3 to 4 hours of sleep each night. I've also lost my appetite completely and have been losing weight. I feel exhausted all the time, and it's hard to concentrate on anything. I just feel worthless.

[Doctor]: That sounds incredibly tough. How has this been affecting your daily life?

[Patient]: It's really impacting everything. I can't do my job properly, I struggle to keep up with personal hygiene, and I don't even want to see my friends or go out.

[Doctor]: I understand. It sounds like this has been very challenging. Have you experienced any other symptoms?

[Patient]: Well, I do feel anxious a lot of the time, and I get really tired. But I think that's mostly because I'm not sleeping or eating well.

[Doctor]: Okay. I'm going to ask you a few more detailed questions about your symptoms to get a better understanding. Is that alright?

[Patient]: Yes, that's fine.

[Doctor]: You mentioned having difficulties with concentration. Can you give me an example of how this has affected you?

[Patient]: Sure. When I'm at work, I can't focus on tasks. Even simple things take forever to complete because I just can't seem to keep my mind on them.

[Doctor]: I see. And how about your feelings of worthlessness? Can you describe that a bit more?

[Patient]: I just feel like I'm not good enough. Like I'm failing at everything, and it would be better if I wasn't around.

[Doctor]: I'm really sorry you're feeling this way. It's important to address these feelings. Have you had any thoughts of harming yourself?

[Patient]: No, I haven't thought about that. But I just feel so low all the time.

[Doctor]: Thank you for sharing that. It's very important you're honest about these feelings. Have you experienced any physical symptoms like headaches, stomach issues, or anything else unusual?

[Patient]: No, not really. Just the tiredness and weight loss.

[Doctor]: Alright. Let's go over your vital signs and do a quick physical examination, if that's okay with you?

[Patient]: Sure, that's fine.

[Doctor]: Your blood pressure is 132/85 mmHg, heart rate is 78 bpm, respiratory rate is 16 breaths per minute, and your temperature is 98.6°F. Your oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Everything seems normal there. Now, let me take a look at your general appearance.

[Patient]: Okay.

[Doctor]: You appear quite distressed and tearful. Your mood seems depressed and your affect is anxious. Your speech is coherent and relevant, but slowed. Your thought process is also slowed, but coherent and relevant. Does that sound accurate?

[Patient]: Yes, that's how I've been feeling.

[Doctor]: Thank you for confirming. I'm going to order some blood work to rule out any underlying medical conditions that could be contributing to your symptoms. We should have the results soon.

[Patient]: Okay.

[Doctor]: Based on everything we've discussed, it sounds like you're experiencing Major Depressive Disorder, Single Episode, and you also have symptoms of Generalized Anxiety Disorder. Does that make sense to you?

[Patient]: Yes, it does.

[Doctor]: For your depression, I'm going to prescribe Sertraline 50 mg to take once daily for four weeks. We'll see how you respond to that. Additionally, you can continue taking Xanax 0.25 mg as needed for acute anxiety episodes.

[Patient]: Alright. I hope this helps.

[Doctor]: I believe it will help. We'll need to schedule a follow-up appointment in four weeks to evaluate how you're doing with the Sertraline. I'll also refer you to Dr. Lucy Martinez, a psychiatrist, for a more in-depth evaluation and ongoing management of your Major Depressive Disorder.

[Patient]: Okay, that sounds good.

[Doctor]: In the meantime, try to seek support from your family and friends. Even though it's difficult, try to maintain a regular sleep schedule and a balanced diet. Minimal physical activity, like short walks, can also help a bit.

[Patient]: I'll try my best.

[Doctor]: Lastly, I'm going to provide you with information on local mental health support services. Considering the limited access in your neighborhood, we can also discuss potential telehealth options for psychiatric follow-up if in-person visits are difficult.

[Patient]: Thank you, doctor. I appreciate all the help.

[Doctor]: You're welcome. Please take the prescribed medication as directed and follow up in four weeks, or sooner if your symptoms worsen. If you have any new concerns or experience any adverse reactions to the medication, contact the urgent care center immediately.

[Patient]: I will. Thank you again.

[Doctor]: Remember to follow through with the referral to Dr. Lucy Martinez. We want to make sure you have all the support you need.

[Patient]: I will. Thank you for everything.

[Doctor]: Take care, and we'll see you in four weeks. Stay safe.

[Patient]: You too, doctor. Goodbye.
